profiles.name: egress
profiles.preparation: closed-loop (each request waits for its response before the next is sent; no scheduled arrival) over the frame protocol, plaintext workload dialler to a mesh peer on loopback; 10 warm-up then 100 sequential connections (connect, first byte, handshake), then one connection of 200 warm-up and 10000 timed 64-byte round trips (tail latency) and one connection carrying one 256 MiB frame (throughput). Baseline arm plaintext-baseline: the same dialler, bound the same way, connects straight to a plaintext TCP peer with no intercept worker, no nft rules and no TLS. Arm composed-mtls: the dialler's flow is registered with the real intercept worker and captured on leg F, which runs mTLS over kTLS to a rustls mesh peer that requires a client certificate; peer tickets disabled; handshake is the enforce duration; resource rows are whole-host scope (the aggregate cpu line of /proc/stat over every CPU and every process, no cgroup figure; each ratio is the class's tick delta over the delta of all CPU time, idle included, user includes nice) sampled across the 256 MiB throughput window; irq and softirq are tick-sampled on this kernel (irq_time_accounting is off, so irq reads 0 and softirq is coarse); memory (VmRSS) and open sockets of the benchmark process are taken at the window's end; connection_concurrency is the peak number of client sessions the family held open (opened and not yet dropped) during that window; forward_userspace_cpu_ratio and return_splice_cpu_ratio are the mtls-out-fwd and mtls-out-ret threads' share of the CPU the process's threads outside the family's own ovbm- threads accrued in that window; the window carries the request one way, so the return pump is the light one; thread CPU is read in 10 ms ticks, so the split is a lower bound at the tick (record note pump_heavy_to_light_lower_bound is the heavy-to-light ratio) and a return_splice_cpu_ratio of 0 means below one tick, because the sustained window carries data forward only; the TLS mesh peer runs on the same host as the agent and may co-limit throughput and tail latency, so the numbers are not pure agent cost

profiles.name: ingress
profiles.preparation: closed-loop (each request waits for its response before the next is sent; no scheduled arrival) over the frame protocol, client to the node's inbound path on loopback with an in-memory guest end; 10 warm-up then 100 sequential connections (connect, first byte, handshake), then one connection of 200 warm-up and 10000 timed 64-byte round trips (tail latency) and one connection carrying one 256 MiB frame (throughput). Baseline arm plaintext-baseline: a plaintext client to a loopback listener that bridges each connection to the same in-memory guest sink, with no TLS and no enforcement. Arm composed-mtls: a rustls client presenting a node-trusted certificate to the real HostMtlsEnforcement serving Routed::Inbound over loopback leg C; the guest transport is excluded, and first byte includes the client side of the TLS handshake; resource rows are whole-host scope (the aggregate cpu line of /proc/stat over every CPU and every process, no cgroup figure; each ratio is the class's tick delta over the delta of all CPU time, idle included, user includes nice) sampled across the 256 MiB throughput window; irq and softirq are tick-sampled on this kernel (irq_time_accounting is off, so irq reads 0 and softirq is coarse); memory (VmRSS) and open sockets of the benchmark process are taken at the window's end; connection_concurrency is the peak number of client sessions the family held open (opened and not yet dropped) during that window; forward_userspace_cpu_ratio and return_splice_cpu_ratio are absent because the relay is asynchronous on shared runtime threads; handshake_ns starts when the enforcement accepts the connection, so it includes the wait for the client's ClientHello (client-side TLS work); the TLS client runs on the same host as the agent and may co-limit throughput and tail latency, so the numbers are not pure agent cost
